note: Container-operation walkthrough by an agent, not a human operator study. Commands ran against disposable Compose projects owned by this walkthrough. Secrets, cookies, mail bodies and links are not recorded; command output is reduced to exit codes and selected sanitized lines.

steps.action: Start owned test dependencies: SMTP relay stand-in, MinIO, Azurite, a separate Postgres 16, and a Caddy reverse proxy on the app host
steps.expected: The fixture project starts beside the installation without changing its services.
steps.actual: Fixture project doc029-rewalk-op-fx started: Mailpit as the SMTP relay stand-in (relay:1025 on the installation's backend network, UI on 127.0.0.1:23342), MinIO (127.0.0.1:23343), Azurite (127.0.0.1:23344), a separate postgres:16 service reachable only on the backend network as extdb, and caddy:2-alpine on the host network serving https://openlaw-rw.localhost:23341 with "reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:23340". Caddy issues the localhost certificate from its internal CA; the browser context accepts that CA, which does not test public certificate issuance.

steps.action: Record the source revision, resolved images, project name, origin and storage location
steps.expected: The identities can be read back from the running installation.
steps.actual: Source 3fa407e3a846559914aa1a63249741f30cfb4f69; project doc029-rewalk-op; origin https://openlaw-rw.localhost:23341; local files in volume doc029-rewalk-op_openlaw-files; images as recorded in the log's images field.

steps.action: docker compose restart does not apply a changed .env
steps.expected: After setting MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and restarting, the app still has the old environment.
steps.actual: After adding MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 and docker compose restart app, the container's MAX_UPLOAD_MB was still empty and a 1,100,000-byte upload was accepted (201).

steps.action: up -d --no-build --pull never applies it; MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 refuses a larger upload and accepts a smaller one
steps.expected: The recreated app enforces the 1 MB ceiling.
steps.actual: up -d --no-build --pull never recreated the app; MAX_UPLOAD_MB is now 1 in the container. The 1,100,000-byte upload was refused with 413 "That file is over the 1 MB upload limit."; a 200,000-byte upload was accepted (201). The Caddy proxy has no body limit configured, so the app's own refusal was seen.

steps.action: An unreadable MAX_UPLOAD_MB falls back to the default instead of stopping startup
steps.expected: MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten starts normally and accepts a 1.1 MB upload.
steps.actual: With MAX_UPLOAD_MB=ten the app started (/readyz 200) and accepted the 1,100,000-byte upload (201), so the ceiling fell back to the 100 MB default. The setting was then removed and the containers recreated.

steps.action: config --quiet validates without printing the expanded configuration
steps.expected: Exit 0 and no output.
steps.actual: docker compose config --quiet exited 0 and printed nothing on stdout or stderr.

steps.action: App and worker share image and configuration with different commands; the engine has no database or credential access; database and engine ports are unpublished; PORT moves only the host port
steps.expected: Inspection matches the article's topology statements.
steps.actual: App and worker run the same image sha256:73b8627b288c6c2a35bbe7906241ad5874253c6bea893e1fb1d539a463cc292f with commands ["node","apps/api/dist/index.js"] and ["node","apps/worker/dist/index.js"]. DATABASE_URL, STORAGE_PATH, BASE_URL, DOC_ENGINE_URL and OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY are identical in both (compared, not recorded). The doc-engine container has no DATABASE_URL, AUTH_SECRET or OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY and joins only doc029-rewalk-op_openlaw-doc-engine. Postgres and doc-engine publish no host ports; the app maps container port 3000 to host port 23340.

steps.action: Document-engine defaults: DOC_ENGINE_URL and DOC_ENGINE_TMPFS_SIZE
steps.expected: The bundled engine URL is http://doc-engine:8080 and scratch space is a 2g tmpfs.
steps.actual: The app's DOC_ENGINE_URL is http://doc-engine:8080. The doc-engine mounts /tmp as tmpfs {"/tmp":"mode=1777,size=2g"} with a read-only root filesystem (true).

steps.action: Sign in through the proxy origin
steps.expected: Password sign-in through Caddy succeeds.
steps.actual: Signed in at https://openlaw-rw.localhost:23341 in the browser; /api/v1/me through the proxy returned the Administrator.

steps.action: Wrong origin: a request whose Origin is not BASE_URL is refused
steps.expected: Sign-in posted with a foreign Origin is refused; the direct port with the configured Origin still works.
steps.actual: Sign-in through the proxy with Origin https://not-the-configured-origin.example answered 403. Sign-in on the direct app port with Origin http://127.0.0.1:23340 (not BASE_URL) answered 403; with Origin set to BASE_URL it answered 200. The app accepts only the configured origin.

steps.action: Upload and download a Document through the proxy origin
steps.expected: Bytes match after a round trip through the proxy.
steps.actual: Uploaded a Document through https://openlaw-rw.localhost:23341 (201) and downloaded it through the same origin; the SHA-256 matched.

steps.action: A live update arrives through the proxy
steps.expected: With the Contract page open in one browser, a comment by a second person appears as a record frame on /api/events and on screen without a reload.
steps.actual: The Administrator's browser held Contract 1 open through https://openlaw-rw.localhost:23341 and read /api/events for that record (HTTP 200). Rowan Operator posted a comment through the proxy (201). A named record frame (record) for that Contract arrived 32 ms later. The comment text did not appear in the visible page within 10 s; the page's timeOrigin was unchanged.

steps.action: local driver: upload and download, file lands in the shared named volume at the default STORAGE_PATH
steps.expected: Bytes match; the file is under /var/lib/openlaw/files in both app and worker.
steps.actual: With STORAGE_DRIVER unset (local), an upload returned 201 and its download matched. The app and worker both see 7 files under /var/lib/openlaw/files in the shared volume.

steps.action: s3 driver: create the bucket first, set the S3 variables, recreate; upload/download new and older Documents; worker processing
steps.expected: New file is written to the bucket; older local file still downloads; processing reaches ready.
steps.actual: Created bucket doc029-openlaw-files in MinIO, set STORAGE_DRIVER=s3 with S3_BUCKET, S3_ENDPOINT=http://minio:9000, S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true and explicit keys, and recreated. /readyz 200. A new upload returned 201 and the bucket now holds 1 objects. Downloads: local 200 match, s3 200 match. A PDF written to s3 reached "ready" in the worker.

steps.action: azure-blob driver: create the container first, set the Azure variables, recreate; every earlier store still reads; worker processing
steps.expected: New file in the Azurite container; local and s3 files still download; processing reaches ready.
steps.actual: Created container doc029-openlaw-files in Azurite, set STORAGE_DRIVER=azure-blob with AZURE_BLOB_CONTAINER, AZURE_BLOB_ACCOUNT, AZURE_BLOB_ACCOUNT_KEY and AZURE_BLOB_ENDPOINT=http://azurite:10000/devstoreaccount1, and recreated. /readyz 200. A new upload returned 201; the container holds 1 blobs. Downloads: local 200 match, s3 200 match, azure 200 match. A PDF written to azure-blob reached "ready" in the worker.

steps.action: Startup validates storage configuration: STORAGE_DRIVER=s3 without S3_BUCKET
steps.expected: The app refuses to start with a storage configuration message; correcting it recovers.
steps.actual: With STORAGE_DRIVER=s3 and S3_BUCKET removed, the app did not become ready (/readyz unreachable (ECONNREFUSED)) and logged "Set S3_BUCKET when STORAGE_DRIVER is s3.". Restoring the settings and recreating returned /readyz 200.

steps.action: Unavailable storage: a wrong S3_ENDPOINT on the retained s3 reader
steps.expected: The app stays ready but the older s3 Document's download fails; correcting the endpoint recovers.
steps.actual: With S3_ENDPOINT=http://minio-unreachable:9000 the app still became ready (/readyz 200) and the local Document still downloaded. The s3 Document's download answered 500 after 0 s. Restoring S3_ENDPOINT=http://minio:9000 and recreating: local 200 match, s3 200 match, azure 200 match.

steps.action: Return new writes to local while keeping s3 and azure-blob readers configured
steps.expected: All three stores stay readable.
steps.actual: Removed STORAGE_DRIVER (default local) and kept the S3 and Azure reader settings. A new local upload returned 201. Downloads: local 200 match, s3 200 match, azure 200 match, localAgain 200 match.

steps.action: DOC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS above 420000 stops app and worker startup
steps.expected: Both processes refuse to start; removing the value recovers.
steps.actual: With DOC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS=420001, the app did not become ready (/readyz unreachable (ECONNREFUSED)) and logged "DOC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS must be at most 420000 milliseconds, so two engine calls still fit inside a derivation job's queue budget.". The worker logged the same refusal (state restarting, Restarting (1) 6 seconds ago). Removing the setting and recreating returned /readyz 200.

steps.action: DOC_ENGINE_COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS above 840000 stops startup
steps.expected: Startup refuses; removing the value recovers.
steps.actual: With DOC_ENGINE_COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS=840001, the app did not become ready (/readyz unreachable (ECONNREFUSED)) and logged "DOC_ENGINE_COMPARE_TIMEOUT_MS must be at most 840000 milliseconds, so one engine call still fits inside a comparison job's queue budget.". The worker logged the same refusal (state restarting, Restarting (1) 5 seconds ago). Removing the setting and recreating returned /readyz 200.

steps.action: An unavailable engine leaves the app ready while processing does not complete; restoring it recovers
steps.expected: With doc-engine stopped, /readyz stays 200 and a new PDF does not reach ready; after start, a new PDF reaches ready.
steps.actual: With docker compose stop doc-engine, /readyz answered 200. A PDF uploaded then was still "pending" after 60 s. After docker compose start doc-engine, a new PDF reached "ready"; the earlier one was then "pending".

steps.action: External database: set DATABASE_URL to a separate PostgreSQL 16 and recreate
steps.expected: The app migrates the selected database, becomes ready, and writes records there; the bundled service stays in the topology.
steps.actual: Set DATABASE_URL to the separate postgres:16 service and recreated. /readyz 200; the selected database reported needsSetup=true. It holds 138 applied migration rows. Creating the fictional Administrator "DOC-029 Sam External" answered 201; that user exists in the external database (count 1) and not in the bundled one (count 0). The bundled postgres service stayed running.

steps.action: Unreachable external database: DATABASE_URL names a host that does not answer
steps.expected: The app does not become ready; correcting the URL recovers.
steps.actual: With the host extdb-missing, /readyz answered unreachable (ECONNREFUSED) and the app logged "Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND extdb-missing". Restoring the external URL returned /readyz 200.

steps.action: Remove DATABASE_URL: the bundled database and its earlier records return; nothing was transferred
steps.expected: The original Administrator and Contracts are present; Sam External is not.
steps.actual: Removed DATABASE_URL and recreated. /readyz 200; Avery Morgan signed in; the Contract list has the same 1 records as before; Sam External does not exist in the bundled database.

steps.action: Remove the owned fixture and installation projects
steps.expected: Both projects' containers, networks and volumes are removed; nothing else is touched.
steps.actual: docker compose -p doc029-rewalk-op-fx down -v and docker compose -p doc029-rewalk-op down -v exited 0; no containers or volumes remain with either project label. The locally built image tags were left in the cache.

stopped.reason: The orchestrator stopped V-C45 mid-run: dev moved past 3fa407e3 and rewrote deployment-configuration.md (SMTP collected as discrete fields). The phases mail, mail-no-from, mail-both, settings-email and keys did not run. No evidence record was written. Both owned Compose projects were destroyed.
